Energy use, cost analysis, and downstream handling or destruction of the concentrated PFAS waste stream are only qualitatively discussed, if at all.

evidence_chunks.section: Data analysis and scenario evaluation, P2–P4

source_limitations: Study focuses on intact commercial RO elements rather than membranes that have operated on PFAS-impacted water; actual PFAS loads on spent elements may be higher.
Leaching tests used Milli-Q water and accelerated laboratory conditions; real system prewashing, cleaning practices, and concentrate-side exposures are not fully represented.

source_limitations: The concentrate originates from IX regeneration rather than a membrane separation step, but the process demonstrates an integrated loop where RO retentate is recycled into a destructive technology.
Detailed energy consumption for the plasma and RO steps and cost analysis are not available from the inspected record.
sources.title: PFAS Destruction in IX Still Bottoms with Plasma Vortex Technology
